newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal opposition says govt squandering chances.
newsitem.headline: Portugal opposition says govt squandering chances.

text.p: The Socialist government is squandering the favourable economic inheritance it gained from the former ruling Social Democrats (PSD), the leader of the main opposition party charged in an interview with Reuters.

PSD leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa also accused the government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres of postponing difficult and potentially unpopular reforms of the social welfare system in the mistaken belief it might be easier after monetary union.
"We cannot forget that beside the inheritance...(this) government has drawn monumental benefit from (declining) interest rates," he said.
Rebelo de Sousa said that private investment was still very sluggish and public sector investment had been "calamitous" over the first half of the year.

The opposition chief put the government's continuing comfortable lead in the opinion polls down to the fact that it had still to take any unpopular decisions in sensitive areas such as welfare spending.
"The Socialists want to leave reform until after monetary union in the belief that what the state gains in lower interest payments will cover the cost of the reforms," he said.
